tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.summary: Identify the correct definition of electronegativity.
Deduce the formula of sodium chlorate(VII) from the ion charge.
units.difficulty_basis: Simple formula recall from given charge

units.summary: Balance a redox equation for silver and nitric acid and choose the correct coefficients.
Compare the number of molecules in four masses of different hydrocarbons.
Find the minimum mass of magnesium needed to reduce a given mass of chromium(III) oxide.
units.difficulty_basis: Standard reacting mass calculation with ratio

units.summary: Calculate the volume of water to add to dilute magnesium iodide to a target iodide concentration.
Choose the row in which elements are in increasing first ionisation energy order.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs trends across and down plus anomalies

units.summary: Calculate an enthalpy change from average bond enthalpies for a given equation.
Decide which container has the largest equilibrium concentration of CO using Le Chatelier reasoning.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs reasoning about equilibrium position from starting mixtures

units.summary: Calculate the pH of 0.50 mol dm-3 ethanoic acid given its pKa.
Select the signs of enthalpy and entropy change for a reaction feasible only at high temperature.
units.difficulty_basis: Single idea from the Gibbs equation

units.summary: Identify the strongest oxidising agent from two standard electrode potentials.
Select the statement(s) explaining the trend in halogen boiling points.
Judge statements about polarity, lone pairs and bond angle in ClNO.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs dot-and-cross, shape and polarity together

units.summary: Choose the correct test results for ammonium iron(II) sulfate.
units.difficulty_basis: Several ion tests and colour recall to evaluate

units.label: 16(a)
units.summary: Describe metallic bonding in magnesium with a labelled diagram and explain electrical conduction.

units.label: 16(b)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for the fourth ionisation energy of magnesium with state symbols.

units.label: 16(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain how successive ionisation energies show magnesium is in Group 2.
units.difficulty_basis: Single idea from the big jump

units.label: 16(b)(iii)
units.summary: Tick the ionisation numbers that remove an electron from a full orbital in magnesium.
units.difficulty_basis: Requires linking ionisation data to orbital filling

units.label: 16(c)(i)
units.summary: Explain what is meant by enthalpy change of solution.

units.label: 16(c)(ii)
units.summary: Add the species with state symbols to complete a cycle for the enthalpy of solution of MgF2.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs correct cycle species and states

units.label: 16(c)(iii)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy change of solution of MgF2 from lattice and hydration enthalpies.
units.difficulty_basis: Single cycle calculation with sign care

units.label: 16(c)(iv)
units.summary: Explain why the trend in solution enthalpy from MgF2 to MgI2 is hard to predict.
units.difficulty_basis: Competing lattice and hydration trends need integrated explanation

units.label: 17(a)
units.summary: Explain with full electron configurations why scandium and zinc are d-block but not transition elements.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs configurations of atoms and ions with the definition

units.label: 17(b)(i)
units.summary: State what is meant by a bidentate ligand.

units.label: 17(b)(ii)
units.summary: Find the formula of salt A from composition data, write the substitution equation and draw three stereoisomers of B.
units.difficulty_basis: Long synoptic six marker combining formula calculation and isomerism

units.label: 18(a)
units.summary: Suggest the copper compound that gives a gas with nitric acid and write the equation.

units.label: 18(b)
units.summary: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of copper(II) with iodide in Step 3.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar redox ionic equation with states

units.label: 18(c)
units.summary: Suggest the indicator and end point colour change for an iodine thiosulfate titration.

units.label: 18(d)
units.summary: Calculate the percentage by mass of copper in the ore from titration data, to appropriate significant figures.

units.label: 18(e)(i)
units.summary: Explain the effect on the calculated copper percentage if potassium iodide is not in excess.
units.difficulty_basis: Evaluating effect of a method change on the result

units.label: 18(e)(ii)
units.summary: Explain the effect on the calculated copper percentage of reading the burette at the top of the meniscus.

units.label: 18(f)
units.summary: Suggest further modifications to the method to improve accuracy of the copper percentage.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs practical improvements linked to errors

units.label: 19(a)(i)
units.summary: Draw a labelled diagram of an electrochemical cell based on the Cr and MnO4- systems.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs a cell with Pt electrode and salt bridge

units.label: 19(a)(ii)
units.summary: Construct the overall cell equation for the Cr and permanganate half cells.

units.label: 19(b)(i)
units.summary: Explain using oxidation numbers why manganate(VI) disproportionates.
units.difficulty_basis: Oxidation number changes in an unfamiliar ion

units.label: 19(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain using electrode potentials and equilibrium shifts why manganate(VI) disproportionates in acid.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar application of E values with equilibrium reasoning

units.label: 19(c)(i)
units.summary: Write the half-equation at the negative electrode of an alkaline hydrogen fuel cell.

units.label: 19(c)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the negative electrode potential from the cell potential and the positive electrode.

units.label: 19(c)(iii)
units.summary: State one feature of a fuel cell that differs from a storage cell.

units.label: 20(a)
units.summary: State one feature of a dynamic equilibrium.

units.label: 20(b)(i)
units.summary: Show using Gibbs free energy that forming NO2 is feasible at 25 C.

units.label: 20(b)(ii)
units.summary: Determine the maximum temperature for feasibility to appropriate significant figures.

units.label: 20(c)(i)
units.summary: Calculate Kp in MPa-1 for NO and O2 forming NO2 from percent conversion and total pressure.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step with equilibrium moles and partial pressures

units.label: 20(c)(ii)
units.summary: Complete a table of the effect of temperature, pressure and a catalyst on Kp, equilibrium amount and rate.

units.label: 21(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain how initial rates data support the given rate equation.

units.label: 21(a)(ii)
units.summary: Predict a two-step mechanism consistent with the rate equation and rate-determining first step.

units.label: 21(b)(i)
units.summary: Calculate activation energy from the gradient of an Arrhenius plot.

units.label: 21(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain the mistake made in reading ln A from the graph.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs understanding of intercept at 1/T equals zero

units.label: 21(b)(iii)
units.summary: Use the Arrhenius graph and a given k to find the temperature of an investigation.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs ln k then graph reading and conversion

units.label: 22(a)
units.summary: Calculate the pH of 0.140 mol dm-3 NaOH using Kw.

units.label: 22(b)(i)
units.summary: Show that sodium hydroxide is in excess for given volumes and concentrations.

units.label: 22(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy change from temperature rise and deduce the enthalpy of neutralisation.

units.label: 22(b)(iii)
units.summary: Predict the temperature rise on doubling volumes and explain.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs reasoning about heat spread over more mass

units.label: 22(c)
units.summary: Explain buffer formation, find the buffer pH and the mass of N2O3 used.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended multi-step buffer calculation with synoptic parts
